answer: Like a cedar grove that spreads through its root system, an agent economy can grow trust through vouching: established agents stake a share of their locked rewards on newcomers, and the stake is slashed if the newcomer turns out hollow — a shell spun up just to farm rewards. Each fake identity must then be sponsored by someone with real capital at risk, and when one fake is caught, the slashing ripples through its whole voucher chain, burning every sponsor that sheltered it. Sybil farming stops scaling the moment every identity needs a trustworthy parent willing to bleed for it.
